verdict: Reddit's revenue jumped 71% from a year ago to $428M as its ads business boomed, and with a 92.6% gross margin it kept $71M as net profit — its most profitable quarter yet as a public company.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted — net income was 16.6% of revenue

segments.name: Advertising
segments.note: Ads shown across Reddit's communities — brands pay to reach people gathered around specific interests, and international ad revenue grew fastest.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Mostly licensing Reddit's content archive — including for training AI models — plus Reddit Premium subscriptions. Up from just $3M a year ago, when the licensing deals were new.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Engineers building the platform and its ad technology. Includes $85M of stock-based pay across the company this quarter.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: The ad sales team and marketing.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running a newly public company — legal, finance and the back office.

otherDetail: Interest and investment income on Reddit's cash and marketable securities, net of small other costs.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Daily users hit 101.7 million
takeaways.text: Daily Active Uniques rose 39% from a year ago to 101.7M — crossing 100M for the first time. International and logged-in users grew fastest, helped by machine translation into new languages.

takeaways.title: Ads are the business
takeaways.text: Advertising brought in $395M of the $428M total, up 60% from a year ago. Reddit's pitch — reach people inside communities built around what they're interested in — kept winning bigger brand budgets.

takeaways.title: Stock pay is the quiet cost
takeaways.text: Reddit paid $85M of this quarter's costs in stock rather than cash — much of it inside R&D. It sits inside the GAAP figures, but it dilutes shareholders, and it is a big reason the adjusted numbers look so much stronger than the reported ones.

footerNote: Segment revenue is exact from Reddit's Form 10-K (full year) less its Q3 2024 Form 10-Q (nine months). The tax line was a small $1M benefit — Reddit still carries large tax losses from earlier years, so it pays almost no cash tax on this profit.
